title: Unify component state variants, reduce token aliases, and standardize Figma publish workflow
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Objective: Reduce component complexity and runtime confusion caused by duplicated token aliases and fragmented state variants in the Figma library. Scope: buttons, form controls, table rows, and chart legend components. Outcomes: single source of truth for semantic tokens, flattened and documented state variants (default / hover / pressed / disabled / loading), consistent auto-layout constraints to avoid measured shifts when instances resize, and a publish checklist so changes are staged with QA and engineering verification.
acceptance_criteria: All button components use semantic color tokens (e.g., color.primary.bg, color.primary.fg) with no direct hex overrides in component instances
Variant sets for interactive components are consolidated so each component has a single Variant Set named 'states' with exactly the five canonical states
Auto-layout constraints audited and fixed so content-driven width/height changes do not break spacing in production instances
A lightweight migration guide and mapping table (old token -> new token) is added to Confluence and linked from the library
Publish checklist added to Figma library description and GitHub PR template; publish only after design + eng sign-off and integration test run (ENG-2912)
At least one downstream repo (examples/web-app) verified that components pulled from updated tokens do not regress visual snapshots
tasks: Audit token usage across library: collect instances that override tokens (Ava)
Create canonical token alias mapping and propose removal of 24 duplicate aliases (Liam)
Flatten variant sets: rename variant groups to canonical names and retire legacy variant keys (Design team)
Auto-layout normalization: normalize padding and gap values for buttons, table rows, and chart legends (Elliot)
Publish runbook & checklist: document steps + required approvals for library publish (Ava)
Engineering verification: ENG-2912 to validate runtime mapping and run visual regression tests (Engineering)
Create migration PR in examples repo showing token swaps and visual diffs (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/124)
Communication: announce deprecation timeline and provide support office hours during rollout (PM: Nora)
Follow-up: schedule 1-week post-publish review to catch regressions and feedback
decisions: Keep semantic tokens as primary source of truth; alias tokens will be reduced to < 6 global backwards-compatible aliases for legacy themes
Variant naming convention: states (default, hover, pressed, disabled, loading) and suffixes only for density (compact/regular/comfortable) rather than combining both in one variant key
Do NOT auto-merge visual token fixes; require manual publish with design+engineer sign-off and visual regression pass
Adopt library publish cadence of at most 2 non-critical publishes per week and 1 emergency publish path with rollback notes
